items.message: This change addresses a silent failure in the acceptance-assessment phase: the heading regex matched only `Acceptance criteria` while every issue in this repository uses `## Acceptance`, causing #443's run to assess nothing and report nothing, which reads as a passing assessment. The fix has two halves: broaden the regex to match the shorter heading (while deliberately not prefix-matching), and emit a WARNING finding when an assessor is bound but no criteria are found, so the silence that looked…[truncated]
Trailing-colon tolerance is untested against `Acceptance criteria:` variant.
Control test uses `_criteria_ticket()` with no assessor — exercises the wrong axis.

This change fixes a silent no-op in the acceptance-assessment phase: the heading regex missed '## Acceptance' (the form every real ticket uses), so the phase exited early with no findings, making a $17.55 run look like a passing assessment. The fix is a tightened regex, a loud warning when criteria are parsed to zero, and tests for both. From a performance angle, the only executable change is in `tdd.py`: the `not criteria` branch now appends a `Finding` and returns rather than returning bare. T…[truncated]

This change fixes a silent-skip bug in the acceptance-criteria assessment phase: when an assessor is bound but the ticket heading doesn't match the pattern, the phase now emits a WARNING finding instead of returning quietly. It also widens the heading regex to match `## Acceptance` (without 'criteria') and tolerates a trailing colon. The changes are documentation, a regex, a conditional branch, and tests. I reviewed all touched files in full. No trust boundaries are crossed: the regex change ope…[truncated]

This change adds a `assess.no_criteria` warning when an assessor is bound but the ticket yields no parseable criteria, and widens the `_HEADING` regex to also match the bare `## Acceptance` form. Three new tests in `test_platform.py` cover the regex change (positive match, over-match guard, trailing-colon tolerance), and two new tests in `test_implement_tdd.py` cover the warning and its negative control (no assessor → no warning). I checked that the new tests assert the right things — the warnin…[truncated]
Negative control passes a `_criteria_ticket()` but the positive test uses `_ticket()` — if `_criteria_ticket()` also produces no criteria, the control proves nothing.
Trailing-colon tolerance (`(?::?\s*$)`) is tested for `## Acceptance:` but not for `## Acceptance criteria:` — whether intentional is unclear.
